verdict.rationale: Postmark documents a single-send endpoint (POST /email) authenticated with one header. It also offers official SDKs and TypeScript examples covering setup through send. A per-recipient `MessageID` appears in its documented examples, and a community user confirms sending with plain curl POST requests. missing for 10: an explicit list of minimal required fields, a verbatim single-send response showing the MessageID (the evidence shows it only in the batch example), and independent hands-on corroboration of the quickstart beyond a vendor-site testimonial.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send a transactional email with one documented API call — minimal required fields, copy-paste quickstart code, and a message id back for tracking

citations.quote: Send a single email]: POST to `/email` endpoint
All API requests require authentication using the `X-Postmark-Server-Token` header with your Server API Token
TypeScript `Promise.allSettled` batch example with per-recipient `MessageID` and error reporting
Install, shared client, template send, batch handling, webhook payload validation, and repair guide — complete TypeScript path from setup to production
Just old fashioned curl and POST requests to send emails with Postmark.
